nodes.label: RAGStack Slash Commands
nodes.rationale: Slash commands (rag-query, rag-index, rag-status, rag-clear, rag-add) are written as .claude/commands/<name>.md files to integrate with Claude Code's slash command system, allowing users to trigger RAGStack operations directly from the conversation interface without manual tool calls.

nodes.label: MCP Server Registration Pattern
nodes.rationale: RAGStack registers itself in ~/.claude/settings.json under mcpServers so Claude Code auto-detects it on next restart without any manual configuration. The PYTHONPATH env var ensures the ragstack package is importable from the MCP server subprocess.

nodes.label: Shared QueryContext Data Flow Pattern
nodes.rationale: A single QueryContext dataclass flows through all 6 layers instead of passing individual values. No layer imports another layer â€” they all read/write the same object. This decouples layers and makes them independently testable.

nodes.label: Lazy Import Pattern for LLM Adapters
nodes.rationale: All LLM provider SDKs and backend dependencies are lazy-imported inside _get() methods or constructor bodies rather than at module level. This keeps zero-dependency backends (memory, passthrough, rules) importable without any optional packages installed.
nodes.norm_label: lazy import pattern for llm adapters

nodes.label: Cosine Similarity Cache Key Strategy
nodes.rationale: The semantic cache uses cosine similarity on query embeddings rather than exact-match keys so that semantically equivalent but differently-worded queries share cache entries. The optimized_query (from L0) is used as cache key to normalize phrasing variations before embedding.

nodes.label: Anthropic Ephemeral Cache Control Pattern
nodes.rationale: The static system prefix is marked with cache_control: {type: ephemeral} for Anthropic so Anthropic's server caches the prefix across requests. This saves prefix tokens on every repeat call with the same system context, reducing cost and latency for cached prefixes.

nodes.label: BFS Graph Traversal Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Graphify uses BFS (not DFS or vector search) so that retrieval follows explicit structural relationships (calls, depends_on) up to hop_limit depth. Seed nodes score 1.0, BFS neighbors score 0.7. Falls back to GRAPH_REPORT.md content if no seed nodes match â€” ensuring some context is always returned.

nodes.label: Hypothetical Document Embedding (HyDE) Pattern
nodes.rationale: HyDE generates a hypothetical ideal answer document instead of embedding the raw query. The hypothetical document is semantically closer to real documentation chunks in embedding space, improving recall for vector-search retrievers like Chroma, Pinecone, and Weaviate.

nodes.label: Overlapping Line-Window Chunking Strategy
nodes.rationale: Files are chunked with 80-line windows and 15-line overlaps so that code spanning chunk boundaries remains retrievable. The 8KB max chunk byte size guards against minified files bloating context windows.

nodes.label: Lazy Pipeline Initialization Pattern
nodes.rationale: The MCP server delays RAGStack.from_config() until the first tool call (_get_stack lazy init). This prevents expensive startup initialization (API client creation, file loading) when Claude Code merely discovers the server's tool list.

nodes.label: ragstack-docs.json Persistence Store
nodes.rationale: Indexed document chunks are persisted to a JSON file (ragstack-docs.json) and re-loaded on each MCP server startup. This avoids re-indexing on every Claude Code restart while keeping the implementation dependency-free.

nodes.label: GUI Quick Presets Configuration
nodes.rationale: One-click presets auto-install missing packages (ollama, graphifyy) and pull LLM models at preset apply time rather than at pipeline startup. This lets users switch providers without any terminal interaction, with progress shown inline in the GUI Status box.

nodes.label: 6-Layer Token-Optimization Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The pipeline is composed of 6 independently-swappable layers (L0 optimizer, L1 semantic cache, L2 rewriter, L3 retriever, L4 compressor, L5 prompt cache) each backed by an ABC from base.py and multiple concrete backends. pipeline.py is the only file that imports from multiple layers, enforcing a clean dependency hierarchy.

nodes.label: Graphify External Tool (graphifyy package)
nodes.rationale: Graphify is an external code analysis tool (pip install graphifyy) that generates a graph.json representing code relationships. RAGStack's GraphifyRetrieverBackend consumes this JSON; it does NOT generate it. The separation means RAGStack works with any graph-generating tool that outputs the same schema.
